paths.description: Anonymous entry and cookie-consent dialog, representing the first-run landing experience.
Cookie decline followed by the anonymous login form and empty submission, representing the primary authentication journey.
Public account-registration surface after cookie decline, representing the account-creation form archetype.
Long-form public Privacy Policy, representing the content/article template.
Authenticated feed, profiles, messaging, settings, and account-management surfaces were not covered because they require a real Facebook account and user data.

findings.summary: The first-run experience does not follow the requested dark theme
findings.evidence: The light and dark captures are byte-identical (51,708 bytes), and the DOM reports color-scheme: normal with a white body surface despite prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and map every first-run surface, including consent, to light/dark design tokens.

findings.summary: The primary consent action misses minimum text contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured the white “Allow all cookies” label on #1877f2 at 4.23:1, below the required 4.5:1 for 15px bold text.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the primary blue or increase the text size/weight enough to satisfy WCAG contrast in every state.

findings.summary: A full blocking cookie dialog obscures the entire entry experience
findings.evidence: Mobile and desktop screenshots show an aria-modal consent layer before any interaction, dimming and blocking the login page; on mobile it consumes most of the visible page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface where legally permissible and keep optional detail progressively disclosed.

findings.summary: The blocking dialog is custom DIV-based UI rather than a native dialog
findings.evidence: The structure probe finds DIV role=dialog aria-modal=true, not <dialog>; focusable elements behind it appear before dialog controls in DOM focus order.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> with showModal(), a labelled heading, native focus containment, Escape handling, and a clear close policy.

findings.summary: The m.facebook.com entry page lacks a mobile viewport declaration
findings.evidence: At a requested 390px viewport, layout reports a 980px CSS viewport scaled to 0.398 and hasViewportMeta=false, making consent copy and footer links extremely small.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 without restricting zoom, then lay out the page at the actual device width.

findings.summary: The entry components rely on page-level scaling instead of component-level responsiveness
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero @container rules and the 390px capture renders a 980px layout scaled down rather than adapting component geometry.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable login and consent components containment and size-aware container query breakpoints, with media-query fallback where needed.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible on the primary login controls and footer links
findings.evidence: The focus probe successfully focused inputs, Log in, recovery, signup, and footer links, but computed outline was none and box-shadow was none for all sampled controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use :focus-visible to provide a high-contrast focus ring with adequate offset on every interactive element.

findings.summary: Empty login submission provides no actionable response
findings.evidence: After declining optional cookies and invoking Log in with both fields empty, the page remained unchanged with no invalid controls and no alert or live-region message.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native required constraints and keep the user on the form with field-specific, programmatically associated errors.

findings.summary: The primary flow does not expose validation or recovery state for missing credentials
findings.evidence: The exercised empty-submit state produced invalid: [] and alerts: [], so users receive no state change, diagnosis, or recovery instruction.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, announce a concise summary, focus the first invalid field, and preserve entered values.

findings.summary: The mobile authentication route paints too slowly
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 5.3s, LCP 7.8s, Speed Index 8.1s and performance 0.59; the raw-CDP trace independently measured FCP 4.04s and LCP 4.19s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP element, reduce document/resource latency, and remove nonessential work from the first authentication render.

findings.summary: Late layout movement and dimensionless consent images destabilise first render
findings.evidence: The layout observer recorded CLS 0.0857 at about 2.26s; all four consent images lack a height attribute and the images probe flags missing dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image space with width and height/aspect-ratio and prevent the late consent insertion from shifting layout.

findings.summary: The anonymous entry route ships a heavy dependency chain
findings.evidence: The HAR records 41 requests and 2,050,669 transferred bytes, including 1.33MB of JavaScript, 324KB CSS, a 183KB font, and a parser-inserted 289KB stylesheet.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the anonymous route, inline only critical CSS, defer noncritical assets, and tune preload/fetch priorities around the LCP.

findings.summary: Large unused JavaScript payloads are delivered to the login route
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s unused-javascript audit failed with three resources while the HAR shows 24 scripts transferring 1.33MB for a simple login/consent surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use route-level code splitting and coverage data to remove modules not needed for anonymous login and consent.

findings.summary: Authentication and consent controls contain accessibility naming/role defects
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found a role=heading image without aria-level and an unlabeled consent checkbox; the registration probe also shows custom DIV role=button controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native headings/buttons/inputs and provide explicit labels and all role-required ARIA attributes.

findings.summary: Consent action text has insufficient contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies the “Allow all cookies” text at 4.23:1 against its blue background, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust consent button colors and test all interactive states to WCAG AA.

findings.summary: Heading structure and focus treatment are incomplete
findings.evidence: The entry structure contains no h1, uses a DIV role=main, and the focus probe finds no visible outline or shadow on sampled controls; Lighthouse also reports malformed ARIA.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a real page h1, semantic landmarks, native controls, modal focus containment, and consistent :focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: The mobile entry view scales desktop typography down to illegible sizes
findings.evidence: The 390px capture uses a 980px CSS viewport at 0.398 scale; the DOM reports 12px body text, rendering key consent and footer copy at roughly 4.8 CSS pixels visually.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the device-width viewport and responsive type with a readable minimum size and line height.

findings.summary: Viewport handling prevents reliable mobile reflow and restricts zoom on a Lighthouse route
findings.evidence: The CDP entry route has no viewport meta; Lighthouse’s redirected mobile login has user-scalable=no, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and never disable pinch zoom; verify 200%/400% reflow and target sizing.

findings.summary: The mobile login route throws a production JavaScript exception
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading getElementsByTagName) in a first-party fbcdn script.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the null/undefined state in scrollToHeader and add production error monitoring/regression coverage for anonymous login.

findings.summary: Consent images omit intrinsic height and the entry document omits key metadata
findings.evidence: The images probe reports all four PNGs missing height; the DOM has a valid doctype/UTF-8 but no viewport or description, and CLS reached 0.0857.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height, responsive sources, and complete the document head for the actual mobile route.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload listeners and bfcache blockers remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a deprecated unload listener and four back/forward-cache failure reasons on the mobile login route.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload work with pagehide/visibilitychange where necessary and remove bfcache blockers.

findings.summary: The entry route has no meta description
findings.evidence: The DOM probe finds title “Facebook” but description=null; the raw HTML comparison also reports no meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, route-specific meta description that describes login and account creation.

findings.summary: The canonical entry experience is not mobile-friendly at the requested URL
findings.evidence: Links are crawlable, but the DOM and layout probes show no viewport meta and a 980px layout scaled into 390px.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a device-width viewport and responsive layout consistently before redirects and consent handling.

findings.summary: The sitemap endpoint fails and indexing signals are inconsistent across m/www routes
findings.evidence: The entry canonical points to en-gb.facebook.com, robots.txt is available, but /sitemap.xml returns HTTP 500.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a valid sitemap index and align canonical/locale signals across m.facebook.com and www.facebook.com.

findings.summary: The anonymous landing route exposes no structured or social metadata
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found no JSON-LD, microdata, hreflang, Open Graph, or description metadata on the rendered entry route.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/social metadata and only the schema.org markup that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Security headers are strong overall but the CSP and referrer controls have gaps
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, X-Frame-Options and Permissions-Policy are present, but Referrer-Policy is absent and style-src allows unsafe-inline.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or stricter) Referrer-Policy and migrate inline styles to nonce/hash-based CSP.

findings.summary: The pre-consent route contacts Instagram and transfers substantial cross-origin resources
findings.evidence: Before consent, the tracker/HAR evidence records an Instagram XHR plus 2.05MB classified cross-origin from Facebook/CDN origins; no known third-party tracker or cookie was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate nonessential pre-consent calls, document each cross-origin purpose, and delay optional integrations until consent.

findings.summary: Defensive policy coverage is incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers show HSTS, DENY framing, nosniff and a broad Permissions-Policy, but no Referrer-Policy and CSP style-src unsafe-inline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit referrer isolation and tighten CSP without unsafe-inline while retaining nonce-based scripts.

findings.summary: The tested primary form does not present a recoverable failure state
findings.evidence: The empty login submission generated neither native invalid state nor an ARIA alert, leaving the user with no diagnosis or retry guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Build explicit loading/error/retry states and use native validation plus announced field errors.

findings.summary: Missing credentials receive no humane validation feedback
findings.evidence: After empty submission, no :invalid/aria-invalid controls and no alert/live region appeared.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, explain how to fix each field, focus the first error, and preserve user input.

findings.summary: Password and registration fields disable useful autofill semantics
findings.evidence: Login email uses autocomplete="username webauthn", but password autocomplete is empty; all sampled registration inputs use autocomplete="off".
findings.suggestedFix: Use current-password, given-name, family-name, bday, email/tel, and new-password tokens as appropriate.

findings.summary: Account creation uses custom controls with weak native form semantics
findings.evidence: Registration exposes DIV role=button submission and inputs without required constraints; sampled controls use autocomplete=off.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real form and submit button, native required/type semantics, autofill tokens, clear terms, and passkey-ready authentication.

findings.summary: Consent imagery is not delivered with modern responsive image practices
findings.evidence: Four below-fold PNGs have no srcset, no lazy loading, no intrinsic height, and no modern format; images transfer 118KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Use AVIF/WebP picture sources, intrinsic dimensions, srcset/sizes, and lazy loading for below-fold cards.

findings.summary: A simple anonymous login surface performs disproportionate work
findings.evidence: The route transfers 2.05MB and 24 scripts; the trace records two long tasks and 184ms TBT, while Lighthouse flags unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a minimal anonymous bundle and defer analytics/integrations and below-fold consent detail until needed.

findings.summary: The anonymous route exceeds a reasonable cross-origin asset budget
findings.evidence: HAR classifies 2,050,231 bytes across 32 requests as cross-origin from the m.facebook.com start URL, primarily fbcdn and www.facebook.com.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an anonymous-route transfer/request budget, normalize first-party origin accounting, and remove nonessential cross-origin dependencies.

findings.summary: The static first-run route has a large in-memory footprint
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 860,566 nodes and 43.9MB self size before meaningful interaction, disproportionate to a login and consent surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the anonymous component/runtime graph, lazy-initialise consent detail, and track heap/node budgets in regression tests.

taskList.title: Restore true mobile reflow, zoom, and legible typography
Make keyboard focus, semantics, and labels robust
Return humane validation and recovery from authentication errors
Cut anonymous-route JavaScript, CSS, font, and dependency weight
Replace the blocking custom consent overlay with a focused semantic dialog
Fix account autofill, native form semantics, and passkey readiness
Tighten CSP/referrer policy and minimise pre-consent requests
Complete metadata, canonical, sitemap, and social discovery signals
Remove production exceptions, deprecated unload work, and bfcache blockers
